newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on rumours.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Monday on market talk that China had suspended copper imports, traders said.

Reports have been circling the market since the middle of last week that China had suspended copper imports -- which was denied by officials in Beijing -- and that domestic copper traders had been ordered not to sell their red metal to support prices.
An official in Beijing of the China National Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp said they had made recommendations last week that traders not sell, but had made no specific directives.
He said the company was now recommending traders sell.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 24,270 yuan ($2,925) per tonne, rising 600 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 23,800 and a high of 24,320.
April rose 370 to 23,690, May 380 to 23,960, July 630 to 24,300, August 700 the 24,260 and the first traded September contract ended at 24,100.
Combined volume rose sharply to 88,320 tonnes from 34,170. Copper opened higher and gained steadily, with most contracts closing near their intraday highs.
Traders said the market talk boosted the confidence of long position holders and speculative buying was seen.
"Stop-loss and speculative buying were the major factors for the day's rises and all later-maturing contracts breached the 24,000-yuan resistance level," one trader said.
"Technical charts indicate copper will rise further after breaching the key resistance level," he added.
Traders said firm spot copper prices would continue to support futures prices but investors were wary about huge short-term risks.
"Volume rose sharply but open interest dropped, indicating many investors liquidated their long positions at high prices," a second trader said.
"Despite current strong market sentiment, fundamentals are not likely to support futures at these levels for long," he added.
Aluminium ended up. April rose 160 yuan to 16,450 yuan ($1,982) per tonne, May 250 to 16,830 and June 250 to 17,050.
Combined volume rose to 7,370 tonnes from 4,160.
